result: ROOT CAUSE of the :app:rustBuildArm64Release failure that had been blocking the Android build. It is a THREE-WAY version split. gen/android/buildSrc/.../BuildTask.kt:27 hardcodes executable="cargo" and runs 'tauri android android-studio-script', so GRADLE USES THE CARGO-INSTALLED tauri-cli, not the npm one. Live versions were: npm @tauri-apps/cli (outer build) 2.11.1 / cargo tauri-cli (invoked by gradle) 2.12.1 / tauri Rust crate 2.11.1. 2.12.1's android-studio-script reads .tauri/cli-options-server.json, a file only 2.12.1's OWN android build writes; the npm 2.11.1 driving the outer build never writes it. Proof the versions were split: strings on the 2.11.1 binary finds 'android-studio-script' but ZERO occurrences of 'cli-options-server', so the error text came from a binary the npm package does not contain. ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-tauri is dated Oct 9 09:54, which is when builds began failing. The error message blames Android Studio, which is a red herring for a CLI build.

result: FIXED. stripImageMetadata returned bytes AS-IS for HEIF/AVIF, so when the canvas re-encode (the primary sanitizer) failed, a HEIF photo uploaded with EXIF intact -- GPS included. Now detects the payload by the `Exif\0\0` signature the TIFF spec mandates, which is present wherever it is stored (JPEG APP1, TIFF header, or an iloc-addressed item in ISO-BMFF). A container we cannot rewrite is let through only when there is provably nothing to leak; otherwise the upload is REFUSED with a message to re-pick as JPEG/PNG. Refusal chosen over a byte-level HEIF stripper because the Exif data is an iinf/iloc-addressed item, not a contiguous span: splicing it out by box arithmetic corrupts the file, and deleting `meta` is worse since HEIF requires it. MUTATION-VERIFIED, and the first attempt at the tests was inadequate - they covered only the scanner in isolation and the mutant PASSED them. Tests asserting the refusal are the real guard: deleting the refusal fails 2 of 8.
method: vitest x8; deliberate revert of the refusal fails 2 tests

result: The gap was not delivery, it was recipients. Ledger 38 proved end-to-end FCM delivery, but the token lived ONLY in each phone's SharedPreferences: zero references to registering it anywhere, so there was no list of devices to push to. Added POST /grindrx/register on the ping server (axis:4242, public via cam.dominusaxis.com) persisting to devices.jsonl, keyed by Firebase's own install id so no second identifier is invented, replacing on rotation. Client registers from BOTH onNewToken and MainActivity.onCreate -- onNewToken alone fires only on first issue and rotation, so an install that launched once and kept its token would never register. Sender lives at axis:/home/axis/push-sender and deliberately does NOT live in the APK: it needs a service account that must never ship in a binary. Sender uses a NOTIFICATION payload, not data, because FCM data messages are not delivered to a closed app under modern Android background-execution limits and OEM battery managers, while a notification is rendered by Play Services without starting the app. It reads the PUBLISHED release from the Forgejo API so a push can never announce something never released. Unregistered/invalid tokens are pruned, not retried forever.
method: node --check; endpoint exercised live (register OK, missing token 400); gradle compileUniversalReleaseKotlin SUCCESS
